thread:
joel: Heads-up: deploybot blocked promote for service-ingest. GCR mirror reports attestation missing in mirror region (eu-west1). Primary push shows attestation, mirror shows stale TTL. Image: gcr.io/redwood/service-ingest:release-20260323

ci-bot: Build completed. Push to gcr.io succeeded. Cosign attestation attached with timestamp 2026-03-23T07:12:30Z. Local digest: sha256:77aa33bb...

gcr-mirror-bot: Mirror attempt to eu-west1 returned: attestation lookup returned 404 for subject sha256:77aa33bb...; replication recorded but attestation propagation delayed due to region TTL reconciliation job. See mirror-job/4382 logs.

deploy-bot: Promote aborted: attestation not found in target region caches. Policy: require attestation present in all target regions for release tags. Audit id: promote-1766549999.

ingest-ops: Is this the known GCR attestation-ttl bug? I thought we had a mitigation after the last incident.

joel: looks like TTL truncation happened on the mirror side — the attestation TTL was set relative to push time in us-central, mirror job computed expiry incorrectly (timezone/clock skew) and treated it as expired. Mirror still has layer blobs, just not the attestation object.

ci-bot: Correction: cosign attached an attestation envelope with expiry TTL 30d. Mirror job logs show replication of blobs but attestation put failed with validation error: "attestation expired" (timestamp skew 3h).

release-manager: We need to avoid holding the whole release for cross-region attestation lag. Options: 1) temporarily relax cross-region attestation requirement for rolling canary (small blast radius) 2) re-run mirror attestation push to eu-west1 (manual copy of attestation) 3) manual digest pin override for canary 4) pause and wait for mirror TTL reconcile (unknown duration).

ingest-ops: Manual re-push of attestation to eu-west1 is possible. I can fetch the attestation from primary and call the mirror API to put it in the target registry. That should be quick (<5m) and keeps the audit trail if we record it.

joel: prefer manual attestation copy over relaxing rules. We need provenance integrity. Please run the copy and note the operator in audit. Also record change window: 09:30-09:45 PT.

ingest-ops: running fetch: `gcloud artifacts docker images describe gcr.io/redwood/service-ingest@sha256:77aa33bb --include-attestations --format=json > attest.json`

ingest-ops: pushing attestation into eu-west1 mirror via mirror admin API. Response: 200 OK, attestation stored. Mirror cache refreshed.

gcr-mirror-bot: Recheck: attestation present in eu-west1 for sha256:77aa33bb. Replication latency measured 38s for attestation object.

deploy-bot: Re-run policy verification: attestation present in all target regions. Promote starting: release-20260323 -> canary 2% us-central then eu-west1 1%. Audit: operator=ingest-ops, reason="manual attestation copy due to mirror TTL skew".

ci-bot: Smoke checks initiated. us-central canary passed health checks. eu-west1 canary instances spun up and returned healthy within 70s.

release-manager: Adding note to release doc: "release-20260323: manual attestation copy performed to eu-west1 due to mirror attestation TTL skew; no code changes. Follow-up: fix mirror TTL compute and add alert if attestation replication >2m." Filing ops ticket.

joel: filing the follow-up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1201 (mirror attestation TTL skew + alert).

ingest-ops: created the ticket and included logs + replication job patch suggestion. Also added a short script to validate attestation presence across regions pre-promote.

release-manager: schedule: keep canary at 2% for 45m, then ramp if no regressions. I'll notify #customers-notify about the manual attestation operation and that builds are safe.

joel: ok closing for now. please keep eye on infra metrics. thanks all. :thumbsup:

gcr-mirror-bot: Promote complete: canary healthy. Override recorded in registry audit: user=ingest-ops, note="manual attestation copy".
